name: APT29 – APT Threat Map
description: Técnicas de APT29 com cobertura do catálogo (score 3=regra, 2=parcial, 1=lacuna)

techniques.comment: APT29 has used the `reg save` command to save registry hives. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used the `reg save` command to extract LSA secrets offline. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has stolen data from compromised hosts. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has ensured web servers in a victim environment are Internet accessible before copying tools or malware to it. | cobertura: regra

APT29 has leveraged compromised high-privileged on-premises accounts synced to Office 365 to move laterally into a cloud environment, including through the use of Azure AD PowerShell. | cobertura: regra
APT29 used large size files to avoid detection by security solutions with hardcoded size limits. | cobertura: regra
APT29 used UPX to pack files. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has embedded an ISO file within an HTML attachment that contained JavaScript code to initiate malware execution. | cobertura: regra

APT29 has renamed malicious DLLs with legitimate names to appear benign; they have also created an Azure AD certificate with a Common Name that matched the display name of the compromised service principal. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has hijacked legitimate application-specific startup scripts to enable malware to execute on system startup. | cobertura: parcial (ASR/D3FEND)
APT29 has installed a run command on a compromised system to enable malware execution on system startup. | cobertura: parcial (ASR/D3FEND)
APT29 used WMI to steal credentials and execute backdoors at a future time. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used named and hijacked scheduled tasks to establish persistence. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used encoded PowerShell scripts uploaded to CozyCar installations to download and install SeaDuke. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has developed malware variants written in Python. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has leveraged the Microsoft Graph API to perform various actions across Azure and M365 environments. They have also utilized AADInternals PowerShell Modules to access the API | cobertura: regra
APT29 has exploited CVE-2021-36934 to escalate privileges on a compromised host. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used SDelete to remove artifacts from victim networks. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used timestomping to alter the Standard Information timestamps on their web shells to match other files in the same directory. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used a compromised account to access an organization's VPN infrastructure. | cobertura: regra

APT29 targets dormant or inactive user accounts, accounts belonging to individuals no longer at the organization but whose accounts remain on the system, for access and persistence. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has gained access to a global administrator account in Azure AD and has used `Service Principal` credentials in Exchange. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has conducted enumeration of Azure AD accounts. | cobertura: regra
APT29 uses compromised residential endpoints as proxies for defense evasion and network access. | cobertura: regra

A backdoor used by APT29 created a Tor hidden service to forward traffic from the Tor client to local ports 3389 (RDP), 139 (Netbios), and 445 (SMB) enabling full remote access from outside the network and has also used TOR. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used the meek domain fronting plugin for Tor to hide the destination of C2 traffic. | cobertura: regra

APT29 has used a compromised global administrator account in Azure AD to backdoor a service principal with `ApplicationImpersonation` rights to start collecting emails from targeted mailboxes; APT29 has also used compromised accounts holding `ApplicationImpersonation` rights in Exchange to collect emails. | cobertura: regra

APT29 has enrolled their own devices into compromised cloud tenants, including enrolling a device in MFA to an Azure AD environment following a successful password guessing attack against a dormant account. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has downloaded additional tools and malware onto compromised networks. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has successfully conducted password guessing attacks against a list of mailboxes. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has conducted brute force password spray attacks. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has collected emails from targeted mailboxes within a compromised Azure AD tenant and compromised Exchange servers, including via Exchange Web Services (EWS) API requests. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used compromised identities to access networks via VPNs and Citrix. | cobertura: regra
APT29 can create new users through Azure AD. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has exploited CVE-2019-19781 for Citrix, CVE-2019-11510 for Pulse Secure VPNs, CVE-2018-13379 for FortiGate VPNs, and CVE-2019-9670 in Zimbra software to gain access. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has compromised IT, cloud services, and managed services providers to gain broad access to multiple customers for subsequent operations. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used multiple software exploits for common client software, like Microsoft Word, Exchange, and Adobe Reader, to gain code execution. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used various forms of spearphishing attempting to get a user to click on a malicious link. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used various forms of spearphishing attempting to get a user to open attachments, including, but not limited to, malicious Microsoft Word documents, .pdf, and .lnk files. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has use `mshta` to execute malicious scripts on a compromised host. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has installed web shells on exploited Microsoft Exchange servers. | cobertura: regra
APT29 uses stolen tokens to access victim accounts, without needing a password. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used WMI event subscriptions for persistence. | cobertura: regra
APT29 used sticky-keys to obtain unauthenticated, privileged console access. | cobertura: regra
APT29 added Registry Run keys to establish persistence. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has bypassed UAC. | cobertura: regra
APT29 used Kerberos ticket attacks for lateral movement. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has embedded ISO images and VHDX files in HTML to evade Mark-of-the-Web. | cobertura: regra

APT29 has edited the `Microsoft.IdentityServer.Servicehost.exe.config` file to load a malicious DLL into the AD FS process, thereby enabling persistent access to any service federated with AD FS for a user with a specified User Principal Name. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used spearphishing emails with an attachment to deliver files with exploits to initial victims. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used spearphishing with a link to trick victims into clicking on a link to a zip file containing malicious files. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used the legitimate mailing service Constant Contact to send phishing e-mails. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used Dynamic DNS providers for their malware C2 infrastructure. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used multiple layers of encryption within malware to protect C2 communication. | cobertura: regra

APT29 has registered algorithmically generated Twitter handles that are used for C2 by malware, such as HAMMERTOSS. APT29 has also used legitimate web services such as Dropbox and Constant Contact in their operations. | cobertura: lacuna
APT29 has compromised email accounts to further enable phishing campaigns and taken control of dormant accounts. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used residential proxies, including Azure Virtual Machines, to obfuscate their access to victim environments. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used unique malware in many of their operations. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has created self-signed digital certificates to enable mutual TLS authentication for malware. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has obtained and used a variety of tools including Mimikatz, SDelete, Tor, meek, and Cobalt Strike. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has conducted widespread scanning of target environments to identify vulnerabilities for exploit. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used repeated MFA requests to gain access to victim accounts. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has abused misconfigured AD CS certificate templates to impersonate admin users and create additional authentication certificates. | cobertura: regra
APT29 has used Azure Run Command and Azure Admin-on-Behalf-of (AOBO) to execute code on virtual machines. | cobertura: lacuna
APT29 uses compromised residential endpoints, typically within the same ISP IP address range, as proxies to hide the true source of C2 traffic. | cobertura: lacuna
APT29 has disabled Purview Audit on targeted accounts prior to stealing emails from Microsoft 365 tenants. | cobertura: regra
